### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia 9  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.462)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6809371)

**Proposed mechanism:** PKP2 (HGNC:9044) —DISRUPTS→ Desmosome Assembly and Maintenance (GO:0034771); LIPN (HGNC:677) —DISRUPTS→ Desmosome Assembly and Maintenance (GO:0034771); Desmosome Assembly and Maintenance (GO:0034771) —LEADS_TO→ Arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia 9 (MONDO:0012180); Desmosome Assembly and Maintenance (GO:0034771) —LEADS_TO→ Dilated cardiomyopathy (MONDO:0013495). Loss-of-function mutations in both PKP2 (causative for ARVD9) and LIPN (associated with dilated cardiomyopathy) disrupt the critical pathway of desmosome assembly and maintenance, ultimately leading to the respective cardiac phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in PKP2 and LIPN do not affect the structural integrity or assembly of desmosomes, or that distinct molecular pathways are independently disrupted by mutations in each gene. _(variant: Exclusion of common pathogenic variants in PKP2 and LIPN in large control cohorts like gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of desmosomal proteins in cardiac integrity could lead to the development of targeted therapies for both arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia and dilated cardiomyopathy, potentially by stabilizing desmosome function or mitigating downstream effects of desmosome disruption.

---

#### 2. epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to plakophilin deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.410)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-6809371)

**Proposed mechanism:** PKP1 (HGNC:9014) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial cell adhesion and keratin intermediate filament organization; PKP1 (HGNC:9014) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial cell adhesion and keratin intermediate filament organization; Epithelial cell adhesion and keratin intermediate filament organization —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal skin fragility (HP:0001769); Epithelial cell adhesion and keratin intermediate filament organization —LEADS_TO→ Epidermolysis bullosa simplex (HP:0001769). Mutations in PKP1 disrupt the normal function of the epithelial cell adhesion and keratin intermediate filament organization pathway, leading to abnormal skin fragility in MONDO:0013495 and epidermolysis bullosa simplex in MONDO:0011472.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in PKP1 are not found in patients with MONDO:0013495, or if the identified variants do not lead to haploinsufficiency, this hypothesis would be falsified. Similarly, if the loss-of-function mutations in PKP1 are not consistently observed in epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to plakophilin deficiency, the hypothesis is weakened. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 1%) in the coding sequence of PKP1 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of PKP1 in these two distinct skin fragility disorders could lead to the identification of common therapeutic targets or strategies for managing epithelial integrity.
